document.title: Ninive (Nineveh)

references.notes: 82-3-23 (mainly BM 49164-54059). Nine cases. One from the Babylon overseer, sent to Baghdad on 14 October 1881 (dispatch inventory 1882 P 3013, case no. 8); eight from the Abu Habbah overseer (dispatch inventory 1882 P 2766, cases nos. 1-8). Sent from Baghdad on 18 November 1881 (Trustees’ Minutes, 14 January 1882). Receipt reported to Trustees, with brief description of contents, on 25 March 1882 (P 1605). There was no Assyrian material in this consignment, and the many Kuyunjik pieces with this date-number must have intruded from elsewhere, probably 82-5-22. The registrar, in assigning provenances, relied on marks on the tablets: D for Dailem and B for Borsippa, with Abu Habbah pieces apparently unmarked. None are registered as coming from Babylon, though there were 247 such tablets or fragments in the consignment. As noted in the section on excavations, the inscribed stone, 82-3-23, 2252 (BM 22460), was registered as from Dailem though probably found at Babylon. This must cast some doubt on the provenance of some of the “Dailem” tablets, and one may also wonder whether the B abbreviation, taken as Borsippa by the registrar, may not at some stage have been intended to represent Babylon.
